info.name: video-platform
info.description:
Requests for the Video Platform API (`/v1`), built from `api/openapi.json` (generated by Scramble at
`/docs/api`). Each request's description includes the OpenAPI body fields and documented responses,
plus notes on behaviour, and each has tests and a saved example from a real local run.

## Run the full cycle

Folders are ordered as one end-to-end journey: **health → sign up → verify email → login → profile →
create video → upload to S3 → complete → error cases → delete → password reset → sessions → sign out**.
Every step saves what the next one needs in collection variables, so open the **Collection Runner** and
run the whole collection (or any folder from the top down).

Each run registers a new user (`qa.<timestamp>@example.test`), so it can be repeated. Mind the rate
limits: 5 registrations/hour and 5 `forgot`/`resend` emails/hour per IP. Locally, `php artisan
cache:clear` resets them.

## Prerequisites (local)

```bash
make up                         # Postgres, Redis, Mailpit, S3 emulator
cd api && php artisan serve     # or: php artisan octane:start   → http://localhost:8000
php artisan queue:work          # sends the verification / reset emails
```

The email steps read tokens from **Mailpit** (`mailpitUrl`, http://localhost:8025). Against another
environment, change `baseUrl` / `rootUrl` and fill `verifyToken` / `resetToken` by hand from the emails.

## Auth

Collection-level auth is `Bearer {{accessToken}}`; `Login` fills it. Public endpoints override it with
no auth. Access tokens expire after 15 minutes: run **02 · Login & tokens → Login** again if you get
`401` while exploring.

## Conventions worth knowing

- **Idempotency-Key** is required on `POST /videos`, `POST /videos/{id}/uploads` and
  `POST /uploads/{id}:complete`. These requests send `{{$guid}}`; reuse a fixed key to see a retry
  answered from the store.
- **ETag / If-Match**: video responses carry `ETag`; `PATCH /videos/{id}` needs it in `If-Match`
  (`videoEtag` is kept up to date by the tests).
- **Errors** are problem details (`application/problem+json`) with a stable `code`.

## Variables

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `baseUrl` / `rootUrl` | API base (`…/v1`) and host root (health probes) |
| `mailpitUrl` | Mailpit web/API, for reading tokens from emails |
| `frontendOrigin` | Allowed `Origin` for `/auth/refresh` |
| `initialPassword` / `newPassword` | Password at sign-up and after the reset |
| `uploadSizeBytes` | Size of the demo upload |
| everything else | Filled in by the run (`email`, `accessToken`, `videoId`, `uploadId`, …) |

item.name: 00 · Health
item.description:
Liveness and readiness probes. They live outside `/v1` and need no auth. Run these first to confirm the
local stack (`make up`, `php artisan serve` or `octane:start`) is reachable.

request.description: Process is up. Checks nothing.
`200` when PostgreSQL and Redis answer, otherwise `503` with the failing check.

item.name: 01 · Sign up & verify email
item.description:
Creates a brand-new account for this run and verifies it.

`Register` generates a unique `email` (`qa.<timestamp>@example.test`) and a `handle` each time, so the
whole collection can be run again and again. Rate limit: 5 registrations per hour per IP.

request.description:
Always answers `202`, whether or not the email already exists, so accounts can't be enumerated. A new
address gets a "Confirm your email address" email; an existing one gets "You already have an account".

The pre-request script generates a fresh `email` and `handle` for this run.

Always 202, whether or not the email is already registered (no account enumeration)

**Body fields** (from OpenAPI)

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints |
|---|---|---|---|
| `email` | string | yes | maxLength 254 |
| `password` | string | yes | minLength 10, maxLength 128 |
| `display_name` | string | yes | maxLength 100 |

**Documented responses:** `202`, `422`

request.description:

item.name: 02 · Login & tokens
item.description:
Signs in and stores the access token in `accessToken`. Every request that needs auth inherits
`Bearer {{accessToken}}` from the collection. Access tokens last 15 minutes; run `Login` (or `Refresh`)
again when you get `401`.

request.description:
Returns `{access_token, token_type, expires_in, user}` and sets the `refresh_token` cookie (HttpOnly,
Secure, SameSite=Strict, path `/v1/auth`). Wrong password and unknown email both return
`401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS`. Saves `accessToken` and `userId`.

**Body fields** (from OpenAPI)

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints |
|---|---|---|---|
| `email` | string | yes | maxLength 254 |
| `password` | string | yes | maxLength 128 |

**Documented responses:** `200`, `422`

header.value: X-Request-Id, ETag, Location, Retry-After, X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset, Idempotent-Replayed

request.description:
Swaps the `refresh_token` cookie for a new access token and rotates the cookie. The `Origin` header must
be one of `FRONTEND_ORIGINS` (`http://localhost:3000` locally).

**Postman note:** the cookie is `Secure`. Newman and recent Postman versions send it to `localhost`
over http, so this returns `200` locally and saves the new `accessToken`. If your client holds Secure
cookies back over http you get `401` (no cookie), which the test also accepts.

Exchanges the refresh-token cookie for a new access token and a new refresh token

**Documented responses:** `200`

item.name: 04 · Videos
item.description:
Video metadata. Videos are addressed by an 11-character public id, saved as `videoId`.

Every video response carries `ETag: "<version>"`; writes need it back in `If-Match` (saved as
`videoEtag`). A stale `If-Match` is `412`, a missing one on PATCH is `428`.

item.name: 05 · Upload (direct to S3)
item.description:
The full multipart upload, with the bytes going straight to S3 through presigned URLs:

1. **Create upload session** – declares size and type, returns URLs for the first 20 parts. Video → `upload_pending`.
2. **Sign part URLs** – more URLs when needed. The first call moves the video to `uploading`.
3. **PUT part to S3** – sends the bytes to the presigned URL and keeps the `ETag` S3 returns.
4. **Get upload status** – how a client resumes after a crash: S3's list of uploaded parts plus fresh URLs for missing ones.
5. **Complete upload** – sends every part's ETag. Video → `uploaded`.

The demo "file" is `uploadSizeBytes` bytes (default 65536) of the letter `x`, so it's one part. The API
only checks sizes and ETags here; the media worker rejects non-video bytes later. To send a real file,
set `uploadSizeBytes` to its size and pick it as a binary body in **PUT part to S3** (files over 8 MiB
need one PUT per part).

request.description:
Needs a verified email and an `Idempotency-Key`. The video must be `draft` or `upload_failed`, and it
can have only one live session (`409 UPLOAD_IN_PROGRESS` names the one to resume). At most 25 sessions
per user per 24 h. Saves `uploadId` and the first part's URL as `partUrl`.

**Body fields** (from OpenAPI)

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints |
|---|---|---|---|
| `size_bytes` | integer | yes | minimum 1, maximum 10737418240 |
| `content_type` | string | yes | one of `video/mp4`, `video/quicktime`, `video/x-matroska`, `video/webm`, `video/x-msvideo`, `video/mpeg`, `video/3gpp` |
| `sha256` | string | null | no |  |

**Documented responses:** `201`, `422`, `401`

request.description:
Lists every part 1..N once with its ETag. The API checks them against S3, assembles the object and
checks its size. Video → `uploaded`, and one `VideoUploaded` event goes out.

Errors: `409 PARTS_MISSING` (upload them and retry), `422 INVALID_PART_LIST`, `422 UPLOAD_FAILED` on an
ETag or size mismatch (the upload is aborted; start a new one), `409 UPLOAD_COMPLETING` while another
call is finishing it. Retrying after success returns the same `200`.

Idempotent: retries (with or without the same Idempotency-Key) get the same result

item.name: 09 · Password reset
item.description:
Forgot → email → reset. A reset revokes every session **and every access token issued before it**, so
the old `accessToken` stops working at once; the folder proves that, then signs in with the new password.

request.description:
Always `202`. Active accounts get a single-use reset link valid 60 minutes. Rate limit shared with
`email/resend`.

Always 202, whether or not the email has an account

**Body fields** (from OpenAPI)

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints |
|---|---|---|---|
| `email` | string | yes | maxLength 254 |

**Documented responses:** `202`, `422`

response.name: 202 Accepted

header.value: X-Request-Id, ETag, Location, Retry-After, X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset, Idempotent-Replayed

request.description:
**Local helper, not an API endpoint.** Reads the newest "Reset your password" email for `{{email}}` from
Mailpit (http://localhost:8025) and saves the token from its link into `{{resetToken}}`.

Emails are queued, so `php artisan queue:work` must be running. In the Collection Runner this request
retries itself (1 s apart, up to 15 times) until the email arrives. When sending by hand, just send it
again if it says no email arrived yet. Without Mailpit, open the email yourself and paste the `token`
query value into the `resetToken` collection variable.
